alertes.pourquoi: At the pace of the last 7 days (17 buys, 2.4 a day), a silence this long happens 63% of the time: it is ordinary. This is not a fault: every token is read properly and judged properly. Of the last 303 examined, 39 are only SET ASIDE until they reach the required age — they come back, they are not lost. What REALLY stops them, on the other 264 — « pool below the buy floor » : 28% of refusals (setting: LIQ_ACHAT_MIN / MC_ACHAT_MIN) — the panel says it protects: 3% went up against 26% for what was bought (54095 followed) · « no public presence at all » : 23% of refusals (setting: SOCIAUX_EXIGES) — the panel says it protects: 4% went up against 26% for what was bought (3430 followed) · « one holder holds too much » : 13% of refusals (setting: no variable: Whale rule, in the code) — the panel cannot tell yet: 24% went up, about the same as the 26% of what was bought.
alertes.quoiFaire: None of these is the one to move today: the panel says each of them protects, or cannot tell yet. A rule worth moving would show its rejects going up MORE often than what was bought; the share of refusals alone says what blocks, not what costs. The shortage is the chain's, not a setting's. The rules stack: a token has to clear EVERY bound at once, and on this chain very few then remain. The "what becomes of the rejected" panel says, for each rule, what the tokens it set aside went on to do: that is the only way to know whether it protects or whether it costs.
